title: The United States in the Depression, annual 1921-1941: bank suspensions and their deposits, consumer prices, the money stock and its parts, unemployment, and the Federal Reserve's accounts, interest rates and indexes
source: Federal Reserve Bulletin, September 1937, 'Bank Suspensions, 1921-1936', Table 1 (p. 868) and Table 2 (p. 873); Federal Reserve Bulletin, February 1937, p. 112, 'Summary of Financial and Business Statistics' (annual averages); U.S. Bureau of the Census, Historical Statistics of the United States, Colonial Times to 1970 (1975), series D 85-86 (Lebergott's unemployment, p. 135), E 135 (BLS consumer price index, pp. 210-211) and X 410-417 (Friedman and Schwartz's money stock and its parts, p. 992)
series: year; susp_banks: number of bank suspensions, all banks (mutual savings banks excluded), Bulletin Sept. 1937 Table 1; susp_deposits_thousands: deposits of suspended banks, thousands of dollars, Table 2 (1933 includes the banks not licensed after the holiday and later liquidated); cpi_1967_100: E 135, 1967 = 100; currency_bn ... gold_stock_bn: X 410 currency held by the public, X 411 commercial bank deposits adjusted (X 412 demand, X 413 time), X 414 currency plus demand deposits (M1), X 415 currency plus commercial bank deposits (M2), X 416 bank vault cash, X 417 monetary gold stock, billions of dollars, annual averages; unemployed_thousands, unemployment_pct: D 85-86 (the heading: 'In thousands of persons 16 years old and over, except, prior to 1947, 14 years old and over. Annual averages'; 1929-1970 from the Bureau of Labor Statistics), per cent of the civilian labor force; rb_credit_m ... excess_reserves_m: Federal Reserve bank credit (bills discounted, bills bought, U.S. Government securities), the monetary gold stock, Treasury currency, money in circulation, Treasury cash, Treasury deposits with the Reserve banks, nonmember deposits and other accounts, member bank reserve balances (total and excess), millions of dollars, averages of daily figures; cp_rate ... aaa_rate: commercial paper, stock exchange call loans, Treasury bills, long-term Treasury bonds, Moody's Aaa, per cent per annum; stocks_1926_100: common stocks; wpi_1926_100: wholesale prices, all commodities; ip_1923_25_100: industrial production, adjusted for seasonal variation (1936 preliminary). The Bulletin columns cover 1929 and 1932-1936 only.
license: Public domain: the Federal Reserve Bulletin (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) and Historical Statistics of the United States (U.S. Bureau of the Census) are works of the United States government.
notes: All values were read by eye on page images rendered with pdftoppm (the text layers of these scans garble the tables) and are checked by identities in checks/check_ch28.py: deposits = demand + time, M1 = currency + demand, M2 = currency + deposits; the sixteen years of suspensions add up to the printed totals 14,943 banks and $8,511,885 thousand; on p. 112 the sources (Reserve bank credit, gold, Treasury currency) equal the uses (money in circulation, Treasury cash and deposits, nonmember deposits, member reserve balances) within 1 million for every year. E 135 prints 48.0 for 1937, out of line with 1936 (41.5) and 1938 (42.2): it is left empty.
